# `scope_fine_move`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Move the mount axes at a small commanded speed for a duration, then wait for it to stop.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (native handler, 64-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x7f850 (64-bit build); axis command helper speedMoveAxisCmd @0x68870 (rate command, timed-move command, 1440 clamp); wait for stop WaitScopeStop @0x68d10; formatter sites @0x7fa80 (210) |

Requires a connected mount that supports motion (INFERRED mapping of the not-supported check). Optionally compensates the x speed for altitude using a cosine factor, clamps to [-16, 16] when limit is true, divides each axis value by dur_sec and issues live speed-move axis commands with the anti-resonance flag false; the shared helper keeps an absolute magnitude cap of 1440 but its 900..1000 snapping is disabled for these calls. The handler then waits for the scope to stop, so a success reply (result 0) follows the motion. The values reach the controller as its native rate value, written raw with two decimals followed by a timed-move command, with no unit conversion in the guider; they share the number space of scope_speed_move speeds. The physical unit is unresolved (needs a device test). No completion event exists. Mount serial: runs on a worker; its commands were not traced beyond the axis-coordinate read (unresolved).

Side effects: Issues live axis speed commands to the mount and waits for the scope to stop.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_fine_move"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Named object only; there is no positional top-level binding. A nested object {x, y} for speed fails the array check. Unknown members are ignored. [READ] |
| `params.speed` | array<number> | yes | - | Two numbers [x, y] bound positionally to the two axes. Missing or non-array speed is logged and fails with a thread-local formatter code that is not a fixed 104/108. Native controller rate values (same number space as scope_speed_move speeds), passed without conversion after the dur_sec division and clamps; the physical unit is unresolved. Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ] |
| `params.limit` | boolean\|integer | no | true | When true, comparable x/y values are clamped to [-16, 16] after any altitude compensation. Boolean or integer (nonzero is true). [READ] |
| `params.dur_sec` | integer | no | 1 | Duration divisor: each axis value is divided by dur_sec (as a double, then narrowed to float) before the axis command, and the handler waits for the scope to stop. A value of the wrong type keeps the default. No positive-duration validator; zero, negative and overflow outcomes are unresolved. [READ] |
| `params.backlash_comp` | boolean\|integer | no | false | Pass a backlash-compensation flag to the axis command. Boolean or integer. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 210 | Mount does not support motion (INFERRED mapping from the formatter site) | `not supported` |
| 315 | No mount connected | `mount is not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

Move, x/y and altitude errors are diagnosed but their propagation is partly unresolved; thread-local errors may be forwarded with codes this table does not exhaust.

## Example

Request, minimal - speed only; values invented:

```json
{"id":90,"method":"scope_fine_move","params":{"speed":[4,-2]}}
```

Request, full - All optional members; values invented:

```json
{"id":91,"method":"scope_fine_move","params":{"speed":[8.5,0],"dur_sec":2,"limit":true,"backlash_comp":false}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_fine_move","result":0,"code":0,"id":90}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_fine_move","error":"mount is not connected","code":315,"id":92}
```
